first.rationale: Onboarding completion has declined and onboarding simplification previously improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption; signup simplification separately improved SMB activation. This directly addresses two linked current funnel issues with a durable mechanism for qualified revenue. I would verify the onboarding and pricing records because both are highly consequential candidates, while pricing’s long-term value and guardrails require scrutiny amid the competitor response.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%, directly addressing the current declines in onboarding completion and activation while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Signup simplification also previously lifted SMB first-week activation. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified revenue lift was paired with 12% lower 30-day retention and failure to survive the first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment rather than react with promotional pricing. The verified onboarding result improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, while the verified 40% SMB discount increased acquisition but reduced 30-day retention 12% and failed at renewal—directly conflicting with sustainable qualified revenue. The competitor’s deeper cut raises acute SMB churn risk, but it does not establish that matching discounts would create durable value. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn separately and revisit non-discount retention options when verification capacity returns.
